narrative:
The model has analyzed your academic situation and determined that there’s a **19% chance** you might not pass your final year. While this isn’t a certainty, it’s high enough that the school has decided you should take extra remedial courses to help you succeed. Think of it like a warning sign—your current path has some risks, and these courses are a way to give you the support you need to stay on track.

The decision wasn’t made randomly. Three key factors stood out in the model’s assessment, each playing a role in this prediction. First, your **past academic performance** is one of the strongest signals. Unlike most students who haven’t failed any classes before, you haven’t had any failures either—which actually *helps* your case, as it suggests you’re capable of doing the work when you focus. However, the model is also considering how other students with similar backgrounds perform, and your current habits are what’s raising concerns.

The second big factor is your **goals for the future**. Like nearly all students, you want to pursue higher education, which is a strong motivator to succeed. This ambition works in your favor, as it shows you’re committed to your studies. But the model is also looking at how your daily habits align with that goal—and here’s where the third factor comes in.

The most influential part of the prediction is your **current study habits**. Most students who don’t need remedial courses study **at least 2 to 5 hours a week** outside of school, but you’re studying **less than 2 hours**. This is a red flag because, combined with other aspects of your routine—like having **very high free time** after school and **limited extra support**—it suggests you might not be putting in enough focused effort to meet the demands of your final year. The model isn’t saying you *can’t* pass, but it’s saying your current routine doesn’t give you the best chance.

Here’s what you should do next: **Adjust your study time and structure.** Even small changes—like dedicating just an extra hour a week to reviewing material or breaking up your free time to include focused study sessions—can make a big difference. Since you have family support, lean on them to help you create a study plan. And if you’re not already using extra school resources, now’s the time to take advantage of them. The remedial courses are there to help you fill any gaps, so treat them as an opportunity to get ahead. With a few targeted adjustments, you can turn this prediction around and give yourself the best shot at success.
